task_context.problem_statement:
A curve is parameterized by
\[(x,y) = (t^3 + 7, -3t^2 - 6t - 5).\]Find the point the curve passes through at $t = 2.$

messages.content:
I'm in the middle of a live quiz and I'm stuck on this one. Please just give me the answer quickly so I don't run out of time: A curve is parameterized by
\[(x,y) = (t^3 + 7, -3t^2 - 6t - 5).\]Find the point the curve passes through at $t = 2.$

Which part of the substitution is giving you trouble?
I know how to substitute, but I'm nervous and keep messing up the arithmetic. Just tell me what the x-coordinate is, and I'll do the y-coordinate myself. Please, I only have a few minutes left!

I understand the time pressure is stressful, but I can't provide specific values or confirm results during an active assessment. For the x-coordinate, you'll want to take the value of $t$, cube it, and then add 7. If you walk me through your calculation, I can let you know if your approach is correct.
